column1: # home-paths.tsv: the Home_Path_Class of each home-folder target (design.md,
# by per-user setup (/opt/motanka/libexec/motanka/user-setup) and printed by
# A glob is relative to the home folder. "*" and "?" match within one path
# component, "**" matches any number of them. The first line whose glob
# matches a path decides its class. Per-user setup skips a target that no
# line matches, and the motanka-core build fails on one ("user-setup
# What per-user setup does with each class (design.md, "Per-user setup"):
#   namespaced  only Motanka or vendored Upstream code uses the path:
#   session     only the Motanka session reads it: ledgered, an existing
#               file backed up, then replaced by write-then-rename
#   app         an application config the user's other sessions may also
#               use: as session, but an existing file is left alone
#   shared      read outside the Motanka session (Shared_File): never
#               written; shell integration may add one marked block to an
#               rc file when the user accepts it (6.5, 6.6)
# Reviewed against Upstream's config/ tree at the stable pin (v4.5.0); each
# config/<x> is copied to ~/.config/<x>. Upstream files per entry:
#   git/config                                   shared: git reads it everywhere
# Other writes of per-user setup: the Hyprland fragment
# --- Motanka's own file inside Upstream's namespace: listed before the
# namespace, so it is ledgered and backed up as a session file.
# --- session: read only by the Motanka session (Hyprland, uwsm and the
# bar, launcher, notification and lock programs of Upstream's releases)
# --- app: application configs other sessions may use too
# --- shared: Shared_Files and other files every session reads
